senses.definition: To dismiss (someone, especially military personnel) from service.
senses.example: His ninth Legion having mutined neere unto Placentia, he presently cassiered the same with great ignominie unto it[…].
Today, haute couture is finished, snorts [Pierre] Bergé at his most gallic, no more than a licence to flog scent and handbags, and a pastime for bored supermodels and cashiered pop stars.

senses.definition: One who works at a till or receives payments.
senses.example: The chefs never cooked before, the cashiers never cashiered before, the dishwashers never dishwashed before, the waitresses never waitressed before, and the managers never managed before.

senses.definition: Person in charge of the cash of a business or bank.
To work as a cashier (at a till or receiving payment).
senses.example: The employer places more emphasis on cashiering skills. Taking the customer's money has risen in importance to the point where many stores have specialists whose sole duty is manning the cash registers.
